node-1.label: An 81-year-old man presented with cough, fever, shortness of breath, and later developed right-sided ptosis and anisocoria with a miotic right pupil.

node-2.label: An 81-year-old man with medical history of coronary artery disease with coronary artery bypass two years prior, atrial fibrillation on rivaroxaban, heart failure with reduced ejection fraction, stage 3 chronic kidney disease, and type 2 diabetes mellitus (HbA1c 8.1%).

node-3.label: Initially developed cough, subjective fever, and shortness of breath; was treated with azithromycin for bronchitis, then levofloxacin after a right upper lobe infiltrate was found; symptoms progressed despite antibiotics.

node-4.label: Exposure history: spent time at a Northern Minnesota cabin with minimal outdoor exposure; previous missionary work in Colombia ended two years before admission; never smoked and rarely consumed alcohol.

node-5.label: Physical exam: temperature 38.6°C, pulse 130 beats/min irregularly irregular, blood pressure 114/61 mmHg, respiratory rate 22 breaths/min, oxygen saturation 82% improving to >90% with 5 L/min oxygen; diminished lung sounds in right upper lobe and diffuse crackles in right lung base; systolic ejection murmur, mild pitting edema to knees bilaterally; no clubbing, cyanosis, cervical/axillary lymphadenopathy; neurologic and skin examinations normal.

node-6.label: Later developed right-sided ptosis and anisocoria with asymmetrically miotic right pupil, more evident in dark environment.

why.why: All three expert analyses support an infectious pulmonary process, and the negative TB/cryptococcus/legionella/influenza tests plus positive Blastomyces urine antigen and BAL GMS budding yeast point to fungal infection. Horner's syndrome is explained by apical scarring rather than a central lesion. Confidence raised from 0.92 to 0.95.

All expert analyses reiterate the absence of a discrete mass and cytologic proof, while positive Blastomyces/Histoplasma markers and negative alternative infection tests provide a unifying non-malignant explanation. No new evidence supports malignancy. Confidence lowered from 0.10 to 0.05.

Head CT/MRI showing no acute intracranial lesions and expert consensus attributing Horner's syndrome to apical inflammatory scarring make a cardioembolic vascular event very unlikely. Confidence lowered from 0.02 to 0.01.

node-10.label: Blastomyces urine antigen test is positive

node-11.label: Histoplasma blood antigen test is positive

node-12.label: Bronchoalveolar lavage GMS stain shows broad-based budding yeast

node-13.label: Chest imaging shows right upper lobe consolidation and left-sided nodules

node-14.label: No cytologic or imaging proof of a mass is found

node-15.label: Pulmonary blastomycosis with disseminated fungal infection

why.why: All three expert analyses independently conclude that positive Blastomyces urine antigen, BAL GMS broad-based budding yeast, RUL consolidation with left nodules, and negative TB/cryptococcus/legionella/influenza tests strongly support pulmonary blastomycosis with dissemination. The Radiologist additionally notes Histoplasma blood antigen cross-reacts with Blastomyces, further consolidating the diagnosis. Confidence raised from 0.90 to 0.93; pending species-specific culture/chest CT/thoracic MRI leaves a small residual uncertainty.

node-16.label: Tuberculosis, cryptococcus, legionella, and influenza-related tests are negative

node-17.label: Head CT/MRI shows no acute intracranial lesions

node-18.label: Right-sided Horner's syndrome is caused by apical inflammatory scarring from pulmonary blastomycosis

why.why: All three expert analyses explicitly attribute Horner's syndrome to apical inflammatory scarring from pulmonary blastomycosis, supported by RUL consolidation, absence of a mass, and normal head imaging. Confidence raised from 0.85 to 0.90.

node-19.label: Pulmonary blastomycosis with disseminated fungal infection

The Radiologist's note that Histoplasma antigen cross-reacts with Blastomyces further strengthens blastomycosis over histoplasmosis. Confidence raised from 0.90 to 0.93; pending culture/imaging leaves residual uncertainty.

The Radiologist notes that Histoplasma blood antigen cross-reacts with Blastomyces, reducing its specificity for histoplasmosis; BAL GMS broad-based budding yeast and positive Blastomyces urine antigen strongly favor blastomycosis over histoplasmosis. Confidence lowered from 0.08 to 0.03.

Antibiotics (azithromycin, levofloxacin) failed, legionella testing was negative, no bacterial pathogen was identified, and BAL GMS shows fungal yeast; all expert analyses favor fungal infection. Confidence lowered from 0.02 to 0.01.
